name: Restrictor de Envíos España
author: patrolman

sections.description:
Many WooCommerce stores in Spain can’t or don’t want to ship to the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla (customs, IGIC instead of VAT, carriers that don’t reach there, etc.), but WooCommerce has no simple way to restrict this by province — only by country.

Restrictor de Envíos España adds a settings screen inside WooCommerce where you choose exactly which Spanish provinces are excluded, with a shortcut button for the typical case (“Canary Islands + Ceuta + Melilla”) or to sell to mainland Spain only. A customer in an excluded zone:

  • Sees no shipping method available for their address.
  • If they still try to complete the order, sees your custom message and can’t place it.

Features

  • Native settings screen inside WooCommerce > Settings > Restricción España — no separate admin page.
  • Searchable multi-province selector, built from the provinces WooCommerce already knows about.
  • Shortcuts: “Exclude Canary Islands + Ceuta + Melilla” and “Sell to mainland Spain only” (Balearic Islands excluded too).
  • Fully customizable customer-facing message.
  • Double protection: hides shipping methods AND blocks checkout (the latter can be turned off).
  • Compatible with WooCommerce’s High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).
  • Stores nothing on uninstall: clean removal.

Compatibility

Works with any theme and any shipping method (local pickup, free shipping, flat rate, third-party carriers): the restriction runs before rates are calculated, so you don’t need separate shipping zones for this.

The plugin’s admin screens and customer-facing messages are in Spanish, matching the audience it’s built for (Spanish WooCommerce stores).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the .zip from Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate it.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > “Restricción España” tab and choose your excluded provinces.
sections.faq:
Does this affect customers outside Spain?

No. The restriction only applies when the shipping/billing country is Spain (ES).

Can I exclude only Ceuta and Melilla, and still sell to the Canary Islands?

Yes, the selector is free-form: tick exactly the provinces you want, the shortcut buttons are just there to go faster.

Does it work with HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage)?

Yes, the plugin explicitly declares compatibility.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • Adds a small “Go Pro” callout at the bottom of the plugin’s own settings screen, linking to the paid add-on. Shown only on our own tab (never as a site-wide admin notice), and hidden automatically once the Pro add-on is active.

1.0.2

  • Removes “for WooCommerce” from the plugin name itself (Plugin Check flags the trademarked term “woocommerce” in the name even with an allowed pattern like “for WooCommerce” — the recommendation is to keep it out of the name entirely and rely on the description/tags to convey compatibility, which already do).
  • Removes the manual load_plugin_textdomain() call (WordPress has loaded these automatically since 4.6 for plugins hosted on WordPress.org).
  • Documents why two Plugin Check notices about $_GET['tab'] are false positives (already sanitized with wc_clean()/wp_unslash()).
  • Renames the plugin slug and display name to remove the restricted “WC” abbreviation, and translates this readme into English, per the WordPress.org Plugin Directory guidelines.

1.0.1

  • Fixes a fatal error: the settings tab was registered incorrectly and could take the whole site down if WooCommerce loaded its settings classes in a different order. Now registered through WooCommerce’s standard woocommerce_get_settings_pages hook.

1.0.0

  • First public release.
